newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin signs decrees on 49 pct Svyazinvest sale.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin signs decrees on 49 pct Svyazinvest sale.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree authorising the sale of 49 percent of telecom holding company Svyazinvest, the presidential press service said on Monday.

It said in a statement 25 percent and one share would be sold at an auction open to foreign and domestic bidders and 24 percent would be sold in an investment tender open only to Russian participants.
The statement from the press service made no mention of the government's proposed merger of its 38 percent stake in long-distance operator Rostelekom.

The decree is entitled "Measures for the further development of electronic communications and the management of shares, now in federal property, in Svyazinvest, Rostelekom, Tsentralny Telegraf, Yekaterinburgskaya Gorodskaya Telefonnaya Set and Giprosvyaz."

On Friday the head of Svyazinvest said he expected Yeltsin to issue a telecoms decree shortly which would cover the merger of government stakes in Rostelekom and the other companies named in the title of the decree into Svyazinvest, as well as the sale of 49 percent of Svyazinvest itself.
Svyazinvest chief executive Nail Izmailov said he believed the Svyazinvest sale and Rostelekom merger would be contained in a single decree.

But the press service said the president's control department, a sort of presidential audit office, had been ordered to ensure strict control of the conditions for transferring government property to Svyazinvest.
It also said Yeltsin had ordered Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to agree with him the conditions for transferring these shares.

Officials have said the government plans to sell 25 percent of Svyazinvest, which owns controlling stakes in 85 regional telecommunications companies, to foreign buyers and 24 percent to Russians, seeking portfolio rather than strategic investors.

But the 25 percent plus one share stake which would be offered to foreign and domestic bidders would be a blocking minority stake, suggesting the authorities are also considering selling the shares to a strategic investor.
A previous attempt to tender 25 percent and one share of Svyazinvest to strategic foreign investors, won by Italy's Stet Spa in late 1995, subsequently fell through.
The 38 percent stake in Rostelekom amounts to a controlling stake of 51 percent of the voting shares, and will create a single entity in the Russian telecoms sector.
But Rostelekom officials say they expect to retain operational independence after the merger.
